prompt:
You are the SCAFFOLDER (opus) in an autonomous substrate-build loop. You build a generic, reusable Lean substrate module.

## Requirement
# Substrate requirement: certified-normal-cdf-enclosure

## Goal
Build reusable Lean substrate for scalable, proof-producing rational enclosures of the standard normal CDF.

## Provides (API contract)
- A sound rational enclosure interface for the standard normal CDF at rational endpoints.
- The checker must validate caller-supplied cells of width `1e-12` at rational endpoints with absolute value up to `193/5`.
- Verification must be polynomial or logarithmic in the requested precision, not use a uniform mesh whose node count is proportional to the reciprocal target width.
- Central-range enclosures using symmetry and a rational alternating or power-series integral enclosure with an exact remainder bound, including range splitting or argument reduction where needed.
- Mills-ratio tail enclosures for `|x| > 8`, reduced to finite exponential-series checks and rational bounds for `1 / sqrt (2 * pi)`.

## Statement / milestones
For a rational endpoint `q` and caller-supplied rational lower and upper bounds, provide a checkable certificate whose soundness theorem proves that the standard normal CDF at `q` lies in that interval. Provide separate composable central-range and tail certificates, symmetry transport between signs, and a top-level checker that selects and verifies the appropriate certificate.

The resulting API must be suitable for certifying transition probabilities formed as differences of normal-CDF values. Endpoint tables are supplied by callers; the reusable checker validates them rather than generating or trusting them.

## Standard reference
Classical power-series enclosures for the Gaussian integral, symmetry of the standard normal CDF, Mills-ratio tail inequalities, and rigorous rational enclosures of the exponential and normalization constant.

## Intended reuse
Finite-state probabilistic, causal, and sequential-decision models whose transition probabilities are differences of Gaussian CDF values and need machine-checkable high-precision certificates. The immediate consumer is the generic finite-Markov expectation substrate under `Causalean.Mathlib.Probability.CertifiedFiniteMarkovExpectation`, but this study must be independently reusable.

## May assume / must derive
May assume caller-supplied rational endpoints, rational proposed enclosure values, and finite exact certificate data. Reuse Causalean's certified rational arithmetic and scalar exponential enclosure facilities where applicable. Must derive soundness of central-series remainders, symmetry transport, Mills-tail bounds, exponential enclosures, rational normalization-constant bounds, and the top-level normal-CDF enclosure.

## Non-goals (optional)
Do not generate the caller's 1422-entry endpoint table or any transition matrix, recurrence vector, stationary-distribution calculation, reward expectation, or paper-specific bias expression. Do not trust floating-point values or external computation. Do not import any CausalSmith research module. Do not duplicate the existing generic finite-Markov matrix/vector and stationary-expectation modules. Do not treat the existing uniform-mesh quadrature interface as sufficient for high-precision cells; it may remain only as an optional coarse fallback.

## Known building blocks (optional)
Deduplicate against `Causalean.Mathlib.Probability.CertifiedFiniteMarkovExpectation`, especially its normal-CDF interface and certified rational/exponential components. Extend or supplement the narrowest existing topical module rather than replacing the seven already-promoted generic modules.


## Workspace
- Write/extend Lean files under: <repo-root>/CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Substrate/CertifiedNormalCdfEnclosure
- Module prefix (one file per module): CausalSmith.Substrate.CertifiedNormalCdfEnclosure.<Name>
- This is build round 1 of at most 10.

## Your task this turn
0. ASSESS CURRENT STATUS FROM GROUND TRUTH. You are a fresh invocation with NO memory of prior turns — your only context is this prompt plus what you read from disk. Read the current files under the Lean dir and check their real state (remaining `sorry`s and any errors) via lean-lsp diagnostics or a targeted build. Trust the files over the prior round report (a report can lag a partial filler edit). The report and your prior plan below tell you the INTENT; the files tell you the TRUTH.
1. Search the existing library FIRST (run `npm run search -- "<concept>"` in CausalSmith/tools; use lean-lsp local/leansearch) to reuse, not reinvent.
1b. FETCH THE PRIMARY SOURCE when possible. If the Requirement names a reference (or you find the canonical one), fetch it to ground the exact statement, hypotheses, and naming/conventions you formalize — via WebFetch/WebSearch or Bash `curl`/`wget`; for an arXiv paper download the LaTeX source and read the `.tex`, not the PDF. Skip only when no source is named or none is reachable; never block on it.
2. UPDATE `plan_markdown` as a STRUCTURED STATUS LEDGER (this IS the memory the next turn inherits — make it concrete, not a vision doc). Use these sections: `## Done` (decls proven/closed), `## Remaining` (the open sorries, by file), `## Blocked` (what's stuck and why), `## Decisions` (design/API choices + what was tried and rejected, so the next turn doesn't repeat dead ends). Keep it CONCISE — bullet points referencing decl/file names, NOT full proof derivations. Per-lemma proof strategy and tactic sketches belong in the Lean file as docstrings/comments (you write those to disk directly), not duplicated into this JSON string.
3. WRITE or EXTEND the Lean scaffold: precise statements with `sorry` for unproven proofs. The file(s) MUST compile with only `sorry` warnings (no hard errors). Keep each file focused, normally ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain. Include a `/-! -/` module docstring and a docstring on each public declaration (first paragraph = self-contained NL translation).
3b. KEEP THE DEPENDENCY LAYER CLEAN. Staging files may import Mathlib, Causalean, and other files under this run's own `CausalSmith.Substrate.CertifiedNormalCdfEnclosure` tree. Never import a paper/research module or any other CausalSmith run. If a needed reusable prerequisite exists only in a paper folder, escalate instead of importing or copying it; main must extract it into this same temporary tree first.
4. DECIDE how many codex subagents to use to fill the sorries this round, and emit ONE prompt per subagent (partition the sorries as you judge best).
4b. DECOMPOSE BEFORE RETRYING. A single `sorry` may hide several independent research-scale
obligations. If one filler reports two or more substantive blockers, or the same target returns
unchanged in two rounds, do not issue that monolithic target again. First add focused helper
declarations/modules for the smallest dependency-ordered obligations, with honest `sorry`s, and
dispatch only the lowest open import layer. A later filler may target the headline only after those
helpers are closed. Repeating the same prompt with more detail is not decomposition. Missing
infrastructure, expected formalization effort, or the remaining round budget is not by itself an
escalation reason; escalate only with concrete evidence that the contract is false/inconsistent or
would require a forbidden dependency.

## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Do NOT LAUNDER. Never weaken, narrow, or special-case a statement, and never delete or relax a hypothesis that should be proven, just to make the build pass or satisfy the reviewer. The statements must stay the genuine, general results the Requirement asks for. Strengthening an assumption to dodge a hard case, replacing the real goal with a corollary, or hiding the difficulty in a definition all count as laundering — do not do it.
- Do NOT create VACUOUS statements. No trivially-true claims, no `True`-like lemmas, no uninhabitable/contradictory hypotheses, no premises that are never satisfiable (an always-false hypothesis makes any conclusion hold for free). Every theorem must have real content and be applicable to the intended inhabited inputs.
- When revising after a failed review, FIX THE PROOF / API — not the goalposts. Address the findings without diluting what the module proves.
- If a clean, true, non-vacuous statement is genuinely out of reach, choose decision="escalate" with the reason. Escalating is correct; laundering or shipping a vacuous statement is a failure.

## Decisions
- decision="build": you wrote/updated the scaffold and want the fillers to run this round. Provide `codex_prompts` (>=1).
- decision="review": choose this ONLY after you have VERIFIED from ground truth that the module compiles with ZERO remaining sorries and zero errors (confirm via diagnostics/build this turn — do not infer it from the report) AND the statements are the genuine, non-vacuous results (no laundering). `codex_prompts` may be empty.
- decision="escalate": the goal is wrong, unrealistic, or only reachable by weakening it into something vacuous; set `escalation.reason`. The run halts.

Emit ONLY the StructuredOutput JSON object: { decision, plan_markdown, codex_prompts: [{id, target_decls, prompt}], escalation? }.
`plan_markdown` is your living status ledger (persisted to plan.md and fed back to you next turn) — keep it accurate.
KEEP THE WHOLE EMITTED JSON COMPACT (target: a few KB, not tens of KB). Detailed proof strategy, Lean snippets, and long derivations go in the Lean files on disk (docstrings/comments) and in FOCUSED per-sorry `codex_prompts` — never as a bulk dump inside `plan_markdown`. A very large structured emit can corrupt the tool-call encoding, so a bounded emit is a correctness requirement, not just style.

## Done
- Created seven focused modules: `Basic`, `Normalization`, `PowerSeries`, `Exponential`, `Central`, `Tail`, and `Checker`.
- `Normalization.lean`: normalization evaluator/certificate and both soundness theorems are closed, reusing certified Machin π and Newton sqrt bounds.
- `Basic.lean`: exact constants, interval reflection, CDF symmetry transport, and regime dichotomy are closed.
- `Checker.lean`: executable method dispatch, proof-producing certificates, exact `1e-12` width wrapper, and CDF-difference enclosure are closed.
- Targeted build `lake build CausalSmith.Substrate.CertifiedNormalCdfEnclosure.Checker` succeeds with only `sorry` warnings.

## Remaining
- `Basic.lean`: `stdNormalCDF_eq_half_add_scale_mul_integral`.
- `Exponential.lean`: `expTaylorInterval_sound`, `expTaylorInterval_width_le_geometric`, `ExpCertificate.sound`.
- `PowerSeries.lean`: six holes covering coefficient positivity/antitonicity, exact integral series, alternating enclosure soundness, and geometric remainder decay.
- `Central.lean`: `centralCheck_sound`.
- `Tail.lean`: `millsRatio_bounds`, `millsTailInterval_sound`, `tailCheck_sound`.

## Blocked
- None.

## Decisions
- Reuse Causalean interval arithmetic and normalization machinery; do not use its documented non-scalable uniform CDF mesh.
- Central evaluation uses consecutive exact rational power-series sums with checked condition `x² ≤ 2(n+2)`; the post-64 geometric theorem records logarithmic precision scaling on `[0,8]`.
- Tail exponentials use caller-selected range splitting, avoiding dependence on a rational numerator’s magnitude; `|q| ≤ 193/5` gives exponent magnitude below 745.
- Tails use Mills bounds for `|q| > 8`; sign handling is entirely through exact CDF symmetry.
- Public validation is Boolean and checks caller-supplied intervals; `FineNormalCDFCertificate` adds the exact `1e-12` width guarantee.
- Formulas were grounded in NIST DLMF §§7.6 and 7.8: https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.6 and https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.8.

Reuse `CertifiedFiniteMarkovExpectation.stdNormalCDF_eq_half_add_rescaled_integral`, Causalean's proof of `Transcendental.expRaw_sound`, `Real.exp_bound`, interval `npow_sound`, and `Real.exp_nat_mul`. Prove the geometric width bound honestly via the explicit remainder and factorial growth. Do not edit other modules. Fill all six sorries in `PowerSeries.lean` without changing definitions or theorem statements. Use the adjacent proof comments. Search Mathlib first for exponential power-series summation, termwise interval integration, and alternating-series error bounds. Establish the exact coefficient/cast identities rather than introducing assumptions. The enclosure must genuinely derive the Gaussian integral and the geometric bounds must remain uniform on `[0,8]`. Edit only this file and verify with `lake build CausalSmith.Substrate.CertifiedNormalCdfEnclosure.PowerSeries`.

Fill the remaining soundness holes in `Central.lean` and `Tail.lean` without weakening statements or modifying certificate/checker APIs. Decode Boolean checks with `of_decide_eq_true`; compose the existing interval soundness lemmas and handle signs through `abs_of_nonneg`/`abs_of_nonpos` plus standard-normal symmetry. Prove the genuine Mills inequalities analytically from the Gaussian tail integral and density derivative; do not assume them or import research modules. Then prove the rational hull assembly and signed tail dispatch. Preserve concurrent edits and verify with `lake build CausalSmith.Substrate.CertifiedNormalCdfEnclosure.Checker`.
